residual_risks.description: Tier 2 always returns passed=True in MVP stub. When v0.2 implements verify_cmd execution, the implementation must correctly return passed=False for failing commands, otherwise the 'no bypass' rule in close_task becomes meaningless.
residual_risks.evidence: harness/__init__.py:_verify_tier2() line 139: passed=True always returned regardless of verify_cmd content

residual_risks.description: close_task and done CLI commands lack a pre-check for task status. An ABANDONED task can be 'closed' back to COMPLETED if the user calls `mem0 done abandoned_task` (though this would fail at Tier 1 if todos are incomplete). No guard prevents closing a task in non-IN_PROGRESS state.
residual_risks.evidence: cli.py:done() and cli.py:close() do not validate current status before calling service.close_task()

testing_gaps.description: No integration test for the close_task atomicity: verifying that close_task raises RuntimeError when Tier 1 fails (pending todos), and verifying status remains unchanged after failed close attempt.
testing_gaps.suggested_test: test_close_task_raises_on_tier1_failure: create task with incomplete todos, call close_task, assert RuntimeError raised, assert task status is still IN_PROGRESS (not COMPLETED)

testing_gaps.description: No unit test for update_session with concurrent writes to session.md. While safe_write uses optimistic locking for task.md, session.md uses plain append — concurrent appends from multiple processes could result in interleaved writes.
testing_gaps.suggested_test: test_update_session_concurrent_append: simulate concurrent update_session calls and verify turn markers are not interleaved
